domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Equalize fraction units
skills.definition: Rewrite quantities so their fractional parts are directly comparable for subtraction by finding a common denominator, creating equivalent fractions, and when needed rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over the relevant denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step finds an LCD/common denominator and converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions.
Tag when mixed-number fractional parts are rewritten into matching denominator form before subtraction.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/d specifically to align fractional units for subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no denominator-based rewriting is performed.
Do not tag conversion of a nonstandard mixed number with an improper fractional part into a standard mixed number; that is S02.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun; that is S04.
Do not tag the arithmetic subtraction itself; that is S03.

skills.name: Normalize number form
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into a standard usable subtraction form, such as expressing a whole number with a zero fractional part or converting an improper mixed number to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is rewritten as an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/d for mixed-number or fraction subtraction when the step's main purpose is number-form setup rather than denominator conversion.
Tag when a quantity is explicitly decomposed into whole and fractional parts to place it into a usable subtraction form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary common-denominator conversion of fractions; that is S01.
Do not tag subtraction of whole parts, fractional parts, or numerators once the form is already set; that is S03.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping of 1 whole into fractional units during subtraction; that is S04.
Do not tag final simplification or final answer formatting unless it is part of the normalization itself.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Perform the subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators of like fractions and subtracting whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted for fractions with the same denominator.
Tag when whole-number parts and fractional parts of mixed numbers are subtracted separately after setup is complete.
Tag when a step computes an intermediate difference such as a negative fractional part before any regrouping is applied.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is to create common denominators or equivalent fractions; that is S01.
Do not tag normalization or rewriting into standard subtraction form; that is S02.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping steps that trade 1 whole for fractional units; that is S04.
Do not tag simplification-only or final-formatting-only steps after arithmetic is complete; those are S04.

skills.name: Regroup and finalize
skills.definition: Resolve subtraction results that require restructuring by borrowing 1 whole into fractional units and/or simplify and express the result in lowest terms as a fraction, mixed number, or integer.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when 1 is borrowed from the whole part and rewritten as denominator-over-denominator or equivalent fractional units.
Tag when regrouping is used because the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
Tag when a fraction result is reduced to lowest terms, including simplifying 0/d to 0 or a whole-plus-zero-fraction result to an integer.
Tag when whole and fractional parts are combined into the final mixed number or integer form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag straightforward subtraction that does not involve regrouping, simplification, or final expression; that is S03.
Do not tag initial denominator alignment; that is S01.
Do not tag initial normalization of a whole number or improper mixed number before subtraction; that is S02.
